assessment_summary: At line 40, the proof claims to resolve the inequality for $p, q \in \R_{\ge 0}$, which includes $p=0$. However, in line 43, it defines the function $\phi(x) = x^{q/p}$. For $p=0$ and $q=1$, this requires computing $x^{1/0}$, which is undefined due to division by zero. Furthermore, the earlier section (lines 31-39) only defines $M_0$ via a limit but never actually proves the inequality $M_0 \le M_q$. Even if we assume line 40 contains a typo and was intended to cover all non-zero $p,q$ (such as $p=-1, q=1$), lines 42-43 explicitly define $\phi$ on the domain $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$, which would require evaluating $0^{-1}$, also undefined. Thus, the definition at line 43 is mathematically invalid.
